title: Appendix A.4: abstract dimension-reduction theorem
statement: Appendix A.4 with the additional hypothesis (H0). Let P, n, Q ∈ ℕ, let F be a set of functions φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, and let sing be any map from functions ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to subsets of ℝ^P. Write φ_{y,λ}(x) := φ(y + λx), μH[n] for the (unnormalized) n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P, and say that a sequence φ_k converges weakly to φ if ∫ f·φ_k dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ dμH[n] for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume: (H0) two members of F that agree μH[n]-a.e. are equal; (H1) every φ ∈ F is locally μH[n]-integrable; (A.1) φ_{y,λ} ∈ F whenever φ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; (A.2) for every φ ∈ F, every y with |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_k > 0 with λ_k → 0, there are a strictly increasing sequence of indices k_i and ψ ∈ F such that φ_{y,λ_{k_i}} converges weakly to ψ and ψ(λx) = ψ(x) for all λ > 0 and all x; (A.3) for every φ ∈ F: sing φ is closed; sing φ = ∅ whenever φ = c·1_L for some c ∈ ℝ^Q and some n-dimensional linear subspace L; sing φ_{y,λ} = {x : y + λx ∈ sing φ} whenever 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; and whenever φ_k ∈ F converge weakly to φ, for every ε > 0 there is k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {x : dist(x, sing φ) < ε} for all k ≥ k₀ (the right side being empty if sing φ = ∅). Then either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for every φ ∈ F, or (II) there is an integer d with 0 ≤ d ≤ n − 1 such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for every φ ∈ F and every real α > 0; there are ψ ∈ F and a d-dimensional linear subspace L with sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for all y ∈ L, λ > 0 and x; and, if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for every φ ∈ F and every σ < 1.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n Q : ℕ) (F : Set (Euclid P → Euclid Q)) (sing : (Euclid P → Euclid Q) → Set (Euclid P)), (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ ψ ∈ F, (∀ᵐ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)], φ x = ψ x) → φ = ψ) → (∀ φ ∈ F, LocallyIntegrable φ μH[(n : ℝ)]) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ (y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → lam < 1 → ‖y‖ ≤ 1 - lam → (fun x => φ (y + lam • x)) ∈ F) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ y : Euclid P, ‖y‖ < 1 → ∀ lams : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 < lams k) → StrictAnti lams → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ (sub : ℕ → ℕ) (ψ : Euclid P → Euclid Q), StrictMono sub ∧ ψ ∈ F ∧ (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • φ (y + lams (sub k) • x) ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • ψ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) ∧ ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ x, ψ (lam • x) = ψ x) → (∀ φ ∈ F, IsClosed (sing φ)) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ (L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (c : Euclid Q), Module.finrank ℝ L = n → φ = Set.indicator (L : Set (Euclid P)) (fun _ => c) → sing φ = ∅) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ (y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → lam < 1 → ‖y‖ ≤ 1 - lam → sing (fun x => φ (y + lam • x)) = (fun x => y + lam • x) ⁻¹' sing φ) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ φs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid Q, (∀ k, φs k ∈ F) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • φs k x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • φ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ sing (φs k) ⊆ {x | ∃ z ∈ sing φ, dist x z < ε}) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ sing φ = ∅) ∨ ∃ d : ℕ, d + 1 ≤ n ∧ (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → μH[(d : ℝ) + α] (sing φ ∩ ball (0 : Euclid P) 1) = 0) ∧ (∃ ψ ∈ F, ∃ L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ L = d ∧ sing ψ = (L : Set (Euclid P)) ∧ ∀ y ∈ L, ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ x, ψ (y + lam • x) = ψ x) ∧ (d = 0 → ∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ σ : ℝ, σ < 1 → (sing φ ∩ ball (0 : Euclid P) σ).Finite)
